- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or shows sharp reversal, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for volatility.
- After a price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in subsequent periods; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome over 3–5 periods, consider mean reversion bias — adjust forecast toward recent 5-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., >1.5% avg daily gain), model often lags; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to capture momentum.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misalign with sentiment direction — align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
